ca_turtle_egg.blurb: Turtle Egg is a small pile of boulders in the Hidden Valley part of Joshua Tree National Park, a short distance southeast of the better-known Turtle Rock. It has nine trad lines, all on short faces, cracks and corners. Grades start around 5.5 and run up to 5.10, with most falling between 5.7 and 5.9, so it suits climbers working through the lower grades on gear. The stone is grainy, and several of the descents take some care, so expect to pay attention on the way down as well as the way up.

ca_merriam_peak.blurb: Merriam Peak is a 13,000-foot summit in the High Sierra, the southernmost of three peaks walling in the west side of the Royce Lakes basin, in the range between Piute Pass and Pine Creek. Its main buttress holds long alpine rock routes, and most of the nine climbs here sit around 5.11, with a few easier ones including a 5.7 mountaineering line and one class 2 route. Expect a serious, committing day at altitude rather than a roadside crag.

ca_queen_crimson_dome.blurb: Queen Crimson Dome is a small formation on the plateau east of Gold Dust Gulch, in the Desert Queen Mine part of Joshua Tree National Park's Queen Valley. Nine routes are here, almost all of them trad with a single sport line. Grades run from 5.8 to 5.12, and 5.10 is the most common range, so it is better suited to climbers who already lead at that level than to beginners. The walk in from the mine parking area crosses the gulch and climbs up onto the plateau.

ca_poolhall_wall.blurb: Poolhall Wall is a compact, knobby wall near Whitney Portal, above Lone Pine on the Eastern Sierra side. It sits northeast of The Whale and is reached by continuing past that crag's approach. There are nine routes, six trad and three sport, from 5.8 up to 5.12. Most fall at 5.9 and 5.10. The face is covered in knobs, and the climbing can be run-out between protection, so it rewards steady leading more than it suits a first outing on gear. The wall can be hard to spot from below.

ca_ranger_station_rock_1.blurb: Ranger Station Rock 1 is a single boulder at around 8,400 feet in Long Valley, in the San Jacinto Mountains. Its nine problems are mostly gentle: several are V0 or easier, a couple are V1, and there is one V2 and one V4 at the top end. That makes it a handy stop for newer boulderers or a quick warm-up between longer outings. The boulder is easy to walk past on the way to other spots in the valley, and a pad is advised.

ca_tehachapi_mountain_park.blurb: Tehachapi Mountain Park is a county park about eight miles south of the town of Tehachapi, at roughly 6,000 feet in the high desert. Climbing here is a side attraction to hiking and camping. The crag has nine routes, almost all top-rope with one trad line, on a pillar with walls around 60 to 80 feet tall. Grades go from 5.6 to 5.11, with the middle of the range around 5.8 to 5.10. Tree cover keeps the face shaded, which can make it a useful summer choice when the lower desert is too hot.

ca_eastern_front_the.blurb: The Eastern Front is a newer wall on Table Mountain, along the Sonora Pass Highway, a short way left of the Grotto. It has nine routes, seven trad and two sport, in the 5.8 to 5.11 range with most at 5.9 and 5.10. The face gets sun through the afternoon. The approach is roughly 15 to 20 minutes from the trailhead used for the Welcome Wall, over a talus field. Bolts for the top anchors sit high on the headwall above the columns.

ca_south_wall.blurb: South Wall is one of the main walls at Big Chief, a ridge-top sport area above the Truckee River Canyon near Lake Tahoe, at about 7,000 feet. The nine bolted routes run from 5.10 to 5.11, split between five at 5.10 and four at 5.11. The wall runs from vertical to overhanging. Routes on the left clear a roof early, and the crux can come below the first bolt, so a stick-clip helps. Routes on the right are vertical with small roofs. Expect a walk of roughly 20 to 35 minutes.

_conflicts.ca_eastern_front_the: Stored rock is greywacke, but the parent Table Mountain page (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/105733998/table-mountain) says the rock is latite. Stored value left unchanged and no rock word used in the blurb.
